Armstrong Predicts New Blockchain Finance Companies
On Saturday, Armstrong made the comments on
X
, comparing the potential impact of blockchain with the iPhone’s role in creating new businesses.
"Apple didn’t predict Uber, TikTok, or Coinbase," Armstrong said.
He added, "But the iPhone enabled an entirely new wave of companies."
He argued that tokenized assets could have a similar effect on financial markets.
"We already know the immediate benefits (global access, better utility, 24/7 trading), but a new set of finance companies we can’t imagine will be built on top," Armstrong said.
Tokenized assets are digital tokens created on a blockchain that represent ownership or rights to real-world physical or financial assets.

Blockchain Push Reshapes Global Finance

Japan’s financial regulators and major financial institutions planned to study blockchain infrastructure for real-time settlement of stocks and bonds, targeting a strategy by early 2027 and possible operation in the early 2030s.

The system could tokenize bank deposits held at the Bank of Japan into digital currency for institutional blockchain settlement, while banks and securities firms were already testing tokenized assets.
The move reflected Japan’s broader shift toward digital finance and came after cryptocurrencies were reclassified as financial assets alongside stocks and other instruments.
Last year,
Pyth Data Association
Director
Marc Tillement
said blockchain could transform global financial markets over the next five to 10 years by reducing fragmentation and combining pricing, trading and settlement on a single layer.
He pointed to
Ethereum
(CRYPTO: ETH) and
Solana
(CRYPTO: SOL) as examples, while noting challenges around speed, scalability, data storage and decentralization.
